prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single universally “best” roofing company for every Dallas homeowner — the right choice depends on your priorities (budget, speed, insurance-claim experience, materials, long workmanship warranty, etc.) and the contractor’s current reputation and availability. I can, however, help you pick the best one for your situation. Two quick options:
- If you want immediate help picking a company, tell me your priorities and whether you’re in Dallas proper or a nearby suburb and I’ll pull a short list of top-rated local roofers (I can look up current reviews if you want).
- If you want to vet companies yourself, use the checklist and questions below.

How to pick the best roofer for your replacement
1. Check credentials
  - Liability insurance and workers’ comp (ask for certificates).
  - Local presence and established track record in the Dallas area.
  - Manufacturer certifications (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, etc.) if you want extended warranties.
  - Business license or registration required by your city.

2. Reputation and references
  - Read Google, Yelp, Angi, and BBB reviews; look for consistent patterns.
  - Ask for recent local references and photos of finished jobs similar to yours.
  - Beware of “storm-chasers” who solicit after severe weather and may disappear.

3. Written estimates and scope
  - Get at least 3 written, itemized estimates (labor, materials, permits, disposal).
  - Confirm whether the quote is for full tear-off or overlay, and how many layers they’ll allow.
  - Ask for timeline, daily work hours, and cleanup plan.

4. Warranties and materials
  - Confirm manufacturer warranty and contractor workmanship warranty (get them in writing).
  - Ask which shingle line/grade they recommend and why.
  - Verify who handles warranty claims later (manufacturer vs. contractor).

5. Insurance-claim expertise (if applicable)
  - If you’re claiming through homeowners insurance, use a roofer experienced with claims and willing to work with your adjuster and provide the documentation your insurer needs.

6. Contract and payment
  - Insist on a written contract with start/end dates, payment schedule, and lien waiver language.
  - Avoid large upfront payments (standard is a modest deposit, balance on completion).
  - Confirm permit responsibility — reputable roofers pull required permits.

7. Red flags
  - High-pressure sales, demand for full payment upfront, lack of a physical address, no contract, or only cash transactions.

If you want, tell me:
- Your location (Dallas neighborhood or suburb)
- Material preference (asphalt shingle, metal, tile)
- Whether you’re filing an insurance claim
- Any important priorities (price, warranty length, quick turnaround)

I’ll then compile a short list of well-rated local roofers and what to ask each one (or I can guide you through comparing quotes you already have). Which would you prefer?
